## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (cell.com/trends/cognitive-sciences submission guidelines) and community-aggregator evidence (manusights.com) gathered 2026-05. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High — international authorship; cognitive-science synthesis across global laboratories |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium — accepts non-Western data when articulated within cognitive-science canonical vocabulary |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Medium-High — neurodiversity, developmental, cross-species perspectives published |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Cognitive science synthesis — neural dynamics, memory mechanisms, perception, multisensory integration, embodied cognition, learning and development (per OpenAlex top-10 topics) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong — commissioned model)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must be **review essays presenting balanced accounts of newly emerging or rapidly progressing cognitive-science fields**. Most articles are commissioned by editorial team; unsolicited proposals accepted via pre-submission inquiry but full unsolicited manuscripts discouraged.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Unsolicited full manuscripts typically redirected to pre-submission proposal track; manuscripts that fail the review-essay format are returned for restructuring.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 1 | Primary research outside scope — TiCS publishes reviews, not original empirical work |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | Outside scope |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 5 | Core article type — theoretical synthesis of empirical literature |
| Mixed methods | 0 | Outside scope |
| Meta-analysis | 3 | Quantitative meta-analysis accepted when paired with theoretical synthesis |
| Review essay | 5 | Flagship format |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 2 — third-person scholarly register dominant; first-person occasionally in opinion or perspective-style pieces |
| **Expected density** | Low |
| **Writing style notes** | Cell Press flagship review-essay tradition — accessible to broad cognitive-science audience; conceptual figures emphasized; reference engagement broad but selective (5–10 key recent references foregrounded per topic) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers are commissioned by the editorial team — leading cognitive scientists with synthesis expertise in the proposal topic. Reviewer turnaround ~10 days (high efficiency due to editorial selection). Editorial commission then peer review structure provides quality control while maintaining commissioning model. Common reviewer demands: "Balanced account of contested debates?", "Engagement with most recent (past 4yr) primary literature?", "Clear synthesis-level contribution beyond literature compilation?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Cognitive science synthesis — leading lab heads commissioned by editors | https://www.cell.com/trends/cognitive-sciences/authors |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Low — editorial commissioning selects high-competence reviewers |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | N/A — synthesis venue; methodology-pluralistic in source literature |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | Cell Press flagship; international cognitive-science leadership | https://www.cell.com/trends/cognitive-sciences |

### AI-Research Notes (supplementary AI research, 2026-07-13)

> Added as a **supplementary, independent research pass** — it does NOT overwrite or supersede the Tier assessment above. Treat conflicts as a signal to re-verify, not as an automatic correction. Overall `signal_quality` for this pass: **2/5**.

**AI-research finding (policy):** 此為 Elsevier 出版社通用 AI 政策(適用於 Trends in Cognitive Sciences,未見期刊專屬版本)。允許作者用生成式 AI 輔助語言潤飾、文獻整理、可讀性改善,但不得直接產出正文而未經實質修改,不得用 AI 生成/修改圖像(研究方法論紀錄除外),AI 不得列名作者。投稿時須揭露使用的工具名稱與用途(聲明置於正文末、參考文獻前)。基礎文法/拼字檢查免揭露。TiCS 本身另有一篇 2024 年發表的評論文章'Towards an AI policy framework in scholarly publishing'(cell.com/trends/cognitive-sciences/abstract/S1364-6613(23)00288-7)討論 AI 政策框架,但那是內容文章而非期刊自身投稿規範,故不採用其文字作為政策依據。

**AI-research finding (positioning — what the journal accepts now):** TiCS 是月刊回顧型期刊(review journal),核心稿件『多為編輯邀稿』(约稿),涵蓋認知科學跨學科主題:心理學、神經科學、語言學、哲學、AI、電腦科學。

**AI-research finding (experiential):** 多筆中文來源(科研通/LetPub/小木虫)一致指出『多是約稿』,即多數正式發表文章來自編輯主動邀稿而非公開自由投稿,故傳統『接受率』統計對此期刊意義有限;未找到量化的桌拒(desk-reject)百分比。

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Original empirical research (TiCS does not publish primary data)
- Unsolicited full manuscripts (community evidence: cell.com pre-submission guide 2026-05 — pre-submission proposal preferred)
- Literature compilations without synthesis-level contribution
- Topics outside emerging / rapidly progressing cognitive science
- Failure to engage 5–10 key recent primary references in proposal stage

### Soft Tax

Variable. For established cognitive-science synthesists: low — commissioning track is straightforward. For unsolicited authors: moderate-high — must first pass pre-submission proposal gate; this requires careful editorial-fit articulation and curated reference selection. Review-essay length and format strict.

### Best Suited For

- Commissioned review essays on emerging cognitive-science topics
- Pre-submission proposals from established researchers in rapidly progressing fields
- Synthesis of empirical literature across cognitive-science subfields
- Perspective and opinion pieces on field-shaping debates
- Cross-disciplinary cognitive-science contributions (neuroscience, psychology, AI, linguistics, philosophy)

### Not Recommended For

- Original empirical research (consider Cognition, JoCN, JEP:General)
- Authors unfamiliar with cognitive-science synthesis genre
- Pure single-subfield reviews without cross-disciplinary stakes
- Independent scholars without established publication record (commissioning model)
- Qualitative or autoethnographic work

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Cognition](../psychology/cognition.md) | If recast as original empirical work; top cognitive-psychology venue; Elsevier |
| 2 | [Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience](./journal-of-cognitive-neuroscience.md) | If the work has neuroscience grounding; cross-disciplinary scope |
| 3 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology General](../psychology/journal-of-experimental-psychology-general.md) | If the work is a general-cognitive empirical synthesis; APA flagship |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top empirical cognitive-science venue as "too synthesis-oriented / not enough original data," TiCS is often a better fit because: it specializes in review-essay synthesis; commissioning model rewards established expertise; and Cell Press flagship reputation provides high-prestige outlet for synthesis work.
